---
title: Create a Google Group
---

# Create a Google Group

This runbook creates a real Google group in your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization, with OpenTofu. Nothing here is simulated: the **Apply** tab creates the group, and the last step deletes it again.

## Before you start

- **OpenTofu 1.12.6 or later** on your `PATH`. Runbooks runs `tofu init`, `plan` and `apply` for you.
- **An admin who can create groups**, such as a Groups Admin or Super Admin, to sign in as.
- **A Google Cloud project with the Cloud Identity API and the Cloud Resource Manager API enabled.** Google bills your API calls to it, so you need permission to use its services, which an Owner or Editor has.
- **A Desktop app OAuth client** for Google Sign-In, from that project's **APIs & Services → Credentials** page. Choose its JSON in the sign-in tab, or point `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS` at it before you start Runbooks.

## Sign in to Google

Sign in as the admin, and pick the project from above. The extra scopes let the form suggest your organization's domains and people.

<GoogleAuth
  id="google-auth"
  title="Sign in to Google"
  description="Sign in as an admin who can create groups, and pick the project that has the Cloud Identity API enabled."
  defaultTab="oauth"
  scopes={[
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-identity.groups',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.domain.readonly',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/directory.readonly',
    'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email',
    'openid',
  ]}
/>

## Create the group

Fill in the group, check the code on **Code**, then plan and apply on **Apply**. There's no repository here, so there's no pull request: the code runs in this session's folder, which also keeps OpenTofu's state.

<TfModule
  id="group"
  source="google-group"
  template="templates/google-group"
  path="google-groups/{{ .id }}"
/>

<Admonition type="note" title="If the plan can't find your organization">
The module finds the organization's customer ID from its domain through Cloud Resource Manager, which works only when the domain has a Google Cloud organization. If it doesn't, clear **Organization**, and give the **Customer ID** under **Advanced options** instead. It's on the **Account settings** page of the Google Admin console.
</Admonition>

## Check the group

<Command
  id="show-group"
  title="Show the new group"
  description="Prints the group's outputs from the apply."
  env={{
    GROUP_EMAIL: "{{ .outputs.group.email }}",
    GROUP_RESOURCE: "{{ .outputs.group.resource_name }}",
    GROUP_CONSOLE: "{{ .outputs.group.runbooks_console_url }}",
  }}
  command={`echo "Group:         $GROUP_EMAIL"
echo "Resource name: $GROUP_RESOURCE"
echo "Admin console: $GROUP_CONSOLE"`}
/>

## Clean up

When you're done trying it out, delete the group with the same code and state. This can't be undone: the group's email archive goes with it.

<Command
  id="delete-group"
  title="Delete the group"
  description="Runs tofu destroy on the code the Apply tab ran."
  command={`(cd .runbooks/tf-module/group/group && tofu destroy -auto-approve -input=false -no-color)`}
  successMessage="The group is deleted."
/>
